home.hero_sub: Harvest Compass tells a farmer which mandi pays the most once transport is paid for, and which days are dry enough to harvest. Wheat, paddy, soybean, onion, potato, pulses, vegetables and more. Ask in English, Hindi or 21 other Indian languages, by voice or text.

steps.d: Prices, two weather models and road km, in parallel
Rejects stale, odd and mismatched prices
Changes the plan if a source fails
Ranks mandis by net ₹ per quintal

home.figcaption: Each step streams live. A full answer takes about 12 seconds.
home.problem_title: Most farmers sell at the nearest mandi, or wherever a trader says.
problems: Prices differ from mandi to mandi, and the trip to reach a better one costs money.
Published prices can be days old, or come from one odd lot that doesn't represent the market.
Rain on harvest or transport day spoils the crop. Forecasts exist, but in English and in millimetres.

gets.d: The mandi that pays most after round-trip transport at the farmer's own vehicle rate, not the one with the highest headline price.
Days inside the harvest window when ECMWF and GFS both expect it to stay dry, and the transport day after.
What waiting three days might do, from the real 14-day price trend and rain risk, labelled as a trend, not a forecast.
Which Rampur? How many kg in a sack? What does the vehicle cost? One short question instead of a made-up value.

home.audit_body: Public price data is messy. Before ranking, the agent rejects prices that are stale, inconsistent, far from the mandi's own recent history, or for a different variety, and names each mandi it dropped with the reason. The language model only phrases numbers the agent computed; a checker throws out any number or mandi name it can't find in the facts.
home.audit_link: How the audit and repair work
home.audit_caption: Real lines from the agent's log, 31 Oct 2026: 40 quintals of soybean near Ujjain.
home.measured_body: We replayed 60 days of real prices for 30 real villages in Madhya Pradesh. Each day the agent chose using only what it would have known that day; we then scored it on the next day's real price against simply going to the nearest mandi. Transport assumed at ₹1 per quintal per km.

how.title: Follow one question, from voice to answer.
how.sub: A farmer asks out loud. Seven steps later they hear which mandi pays the most and which days are dry enough to harvest. AI is used only to understand the question and to word the reply. Everything in between is plain maths you can check.
how.question: I have 40 quintals of soybean in Sanwer, near Indore. Where should I sell?
how.legend_code_long: Plain rules and maths, no AI

flow.name: Understand
flow.plain: Turns everyday speech into clear facts. If something is missing, it asks one short question instead of guessing.

flow.name: Plan
flow.plain: Works out what this question needs to know, and where to find it.

flow.name: Fetch
flow.plain: Collects everything at the same time from public sources, and keeps a dated copy of each answer.

flow.name: Check
flow.plain: Throws out prices that are old, unusual or for a different variety, and keeps the reason to show the farmer.

flow.name: Recover
flow.plain: If a source is down, it switches to a backup and says how fresh that data is. It never fills a gap with a guess.
out: Latest stored report, with its date

flow.name: Calculate
flow.plain: For every mandi: the price, minus the cost of getting there and back. The most money left in hand wins.

flow.name: Answer
flow.plain: Writes a short reply in the farmer's language using only the computed numbers, then reads it aloud.
out: Every number matched to the facts

how.rules_title: Five checks before a price is trusted
how.rules_body: Public price data is messy. A mandi that fails a check is never hidden: the farmer sees it under "Mandis left out" with the reason.

rules.v: Price reported more than 3 days ago
Lowest price above the highest, or the usual price outside that range
Far from both the mandi's own last month and today's prices nearby
A different variety or grade from what most mandis nearby report
Mandi town can't be found, so there's no honest road distance

how.switches_body: On the ask page, test switches turn off a source for the next question: today's prices, one weather model, or routing. The agent skips it and the step log shows how it recovers.
how.voice_body: Questions can be spoken in 22 Indian languages and English, and the words land in the box so a misheard word can be fixed. Replies are read aloud in 9 languages and shown as text in all of them.

farmer.name: Farmer
farmer.d: Asks by voice or text in any of 23 languages. No app, no login.

stt.name: Speech to text
stt.d: Sarvam turns the recording into text in the chosen language. The text appears in the box so the farmer can fix a misheard word.

prices.name: Mandi prices
prices.d: data.gov.in: today's prices and 30 days of history for every mandi in the farmer's state.

weather.name: Weather
weather.d: Open-Meteo: daily rain from two models, ECMWF and GFS.

roads.name: Road distance
roads.d: OSRM: real road km and drive time from the village to each mandi.

places.name: Places
places.d: OpenStreetMap: where the village and each mandi are. One lookup a second, results saved.

cache.name: Saved data
cache.d: Postgres keeps every real response with its source and time, so a failed call can fall back to real older data.

understand.name: Understand
understand.d: The AI model turns the question into clear facts: crop, quantity, village, harvest dates, vehicle rate. If something is missing, it asks one short question.

plan.name: Plan
plan.d: Rules pick which sources to call and why.

fetch.name: Fetch
fetch.d: Calls every source at once, with a time limit and one retry, and records each source and fetch time.

audit.name: Check data
audit.d: Rejects stale, contradictory, unusual or different-variety prices, and names each mandi it left out.

repair.name: Repair
repair.d: If a source is down or too few mandis are left: use saved real data with its age, switch weather model, or search wider. Then fetch again.

calc.name: Calculate
calc.d: 7-day median price minus round-trip transport at the farmer's rate = money in hand per quintal. Also the safest dry days and the price trend.

explain.name: Write answer
explain.d: The AI model words two or three sentences in the farmer's language, using only the calculated facts.

check.name: Number check
check.d: Every number and the mandi name must match the facts. If not, the answer is rewritten once, then a fixed template is used.

answer.name: Answer card
answer.d: Best mandi, money in hand, map, comparison table, editable costs, and every source with its time.

tts.name: Text to speech
tts.d: Sarvam reads the answer aloud when the question was spoken or read-aloud is on. A daily limit protects credits.

results.title: What we measured
results.sub: All figures are read from stored runs, including cases where the agent does not beat the simple choice.
results.bt_title: Backtest: 60 days, 30 villages in Madhya Pradesh
results.bt_body: Each day, the agent chose a mandi using only data up to that day, with its own audit and ranking. We scored the choice on the next day's real price at that mandi, against the nearest reporting mandi. Regret is how far behind the best mandi in hindsight it was.
results.ground_title: Grounding: does the model invent numbers?
results.ground_body: 20 varied questions through the whole agent, on 31 Oct 2026. Every number in each answer was checked against the computed facts.

ground_rows.note: The 20th correctly asked to confirm a tahsil
Wrote Badnagar as a different town

results.usage_body: Logged for every question asked on this site. No IP or identity is stored.
limits: Transport in the backtest is an assumed range, not a measured local rate. Live answers use the farmer's own rate.
data.gov.in history lags a day and many mandis skip days; about 30–40% of replayed decisions couldn't be scored.
The ₹50 per quintal close-call margin is a judgement call.
Only mandis in the farmer's own state are compared.
Weather beyond 7 days isn't forecast; those days are shown as having no forecast yet.
Voice accuracy on real farmer recordings is still being measured.

data.fee_body: In Madhya Pradesh, under the Krishi Upaj Mandi Adhiniyam 1972, section 19(2), the buyer pays the market fee and it can't be deducted from the farmer's price, so the seller's fee is zero. Other states set their own rules, so there the answer notes that the market fee is not included. Hammali and weighing charges are set by each mandi committee, so the farmer enters them if they pay them; nothing is assumed.
data.vehicle_body: There's no public source for local truck and tractor hire, so the agent asks the farmer for their rate per km and how many quintals one trip carries. Both can be edited on the answer to recalculate.
data.fail_body: The agent falls back to the latest real stored data and states its age, or to the other weather model, and lowers its confidence. It never fills a gap with a made-up value.
data.privacy_body: Questions and the agent's steps are logged to measure speed and reliability. IP addresses and identities are not stored.

about.title: Public data, put to work for the person who grows the crop.
about.p1: India publishes daily prices from mandis across the country, and global weather models are free to use. But this data is scattered, in English, unchecked, and shaped for analysts. A farmer with 40 quintals still decides with a phone call to a trader.
about.p2: Harvest Compass brings that data to one question asked in the farmer's own language, checks it before trusting it, and shows its working. It covers the crops data.gov.in reports, from wheat and paddy to vegetables, for any village in India, using the mandis that report in the farmer's state. Built for FORGE '26.
